coverage.main: Read all eight pages of the AAAI 2019 version of record (pp. 8973-8980; adds a fourth author, a related-work paragraph and a temporal-mask subsection) and all seven pages of arXiv 1803.02536v1. Tables 1-4 print the same values in both; judgments rest on the version of record.
coverage.supplement: No appendix or supplement is included or referenced.
coverage.excluded_results: Table 3 diagonal cells are white-box. Table 1 (sparsity) and Figure 8 (l2 versus l2,1) are white-box fooling rates on the attacked network. Table 4 applies universal perturbations from training to test videos on the same network, which is cross-input rather than cross-model. Table 2 reports computation time. Figures 1 and 3-7 are qualitative or per-example perturbation traces.

result_groups.locator: Performance and Transferability, Transferability across Models; Table 3 off-diagonal cells (VoR p. 8978-8979)
result_groups.population: UCF101 videos (the evaluated split and number are not stated); perturbations computed on the first N = 20 of 40 frames with an l2 penalty on a CNN+VanillaRNN, LSTM, GRU or average-pooling source; other architectures as targets
result_groups.outcome: fooling ratio: 'the percentage of adversarial videos that are successfully misclassified'
result_groups.evidence: No clean-correct or source-success rule is stated. The white-box diagonal cells are below 100% for VanillaRNN (95.2%) and Pooling (87.3%).

f1.evidence: No clean accuracy of any action-recognition model is reported.

f2.evidence: No clean-correct restriction or explicit inclusion is stated.

f3.evidence: No source-success restriction or explicit inclusion is stated.

f4.evidence: One-decimal percentages without a stated number of evaluated videos.

f5.locator: Methodology Eqs. 1-4; Adversarial Video based on Propagation
f5.evidence: Perturbations minimise lambda times an l2,1 (or, for Table 3, l2) norm penalty minus the loss, with no L-infinity or L2 radius; magnitude is reported only as mean absolute perturbation. This is an explicit design choice.

f6.evidence: The paper links no code. A 2019 TensorFlow repository describing itself as code for the paper exists under an account not matching an author name. Its provenance and contents were not established.

artifact_checks.result: Two results: yanhui002/video_adv ('Tensorflow code for Sparse Adversarial Perturbations for Videos', last push 8 March 2019) and a 2024 third-party PyTorch reimplementation. Neither is linked from the paper; not inspected further or executed; not used for field 6.

bounds_checks.reason: No clean accuracy of the target networks on the evaluated videos, and the evaluated set is not identified.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Only the four-by-four Table 3 matrix is a cross-model transfer result.
